data.title: bn-3rx: Compile layered scenes, metatiles, and semantic tilemaps

data.body: P1 resource safety: atlas bounds validation adds untrusted u32 values with  / . A manifest such as origin=[1,0], size=[4294967295,1] panics in debug and wraps in release, so it can pass this gate and reach wrapped ranges or enormous allocations. This violates the requirement to validate atlas reservations before publication. Use checked_add (or subtraction-based bounds), then add max-u32 regressions that return a normal compile error without creating the output root.

P1 generated-runtime correctness:  explicitly accepts names beginning with digits, but generated Lua emits class/tag/layer names as bare identifiers (, ). Such a manifest compiles successfully and then produces syntactically invalid Lua, so normal build/run consumption fails. Either emit quoted bracket keys everywhere or use a Lua-identifier validator for every bare-key context; add build/run regressions for digit-leading class, tag, and decorative-layer names.

P1 bounds correctness: object dimensions are u32 but are converted with  before checked_add. Values above i32::MAX wrap negative; for example size=[4294967295,1] can yield right=-1 and pass the world-bounds test, publishing an inverted object rectangle and invalid Lua/provenance. Reject dimensions above i32::MAX or perform the bounds math in a wider signed type with checked conversions, with boundary regressions.

P1 atomic-publication/path validation: output preflight rejects only symlinks, not wrong component types. If an existing output root contains a regular file named , validation succeeds; publication atomically replaces atlas/map/Lua first, then fails when  calls create_dir_all on that file. The result is a partially updated artifact set despite the promise that output paths are validated before publication. Preflight every intermediate as a directory and every leaf as a non-directory before the first rename (and add a regression proving no earlier byte changes on this failure); consider a staged directory/set commit for later I/O failures.

P2 evidence correctness: managed optional outputs are never reconciled. Compile a nearest/quantized scene, then switch it to exact:  remains on disk, and  still reports  because it compares only the newly expected list. That leaves false lossy evidence attached to an exact build. Treat absent managed optional artifacts as stale (remove them safely on write and reject them in --check), with a lossy-to-exact regression.

P1 resource bounds: the 64 MiB PNG limit is per file, but the manifest has no aggregate layer/cell budget and  retains a full  grid (plus lossy heat buffers) for every layer. Repeating a large valid layer can consume gigabytes before atlas capacity or decorative-map bounds are checked; exact mapping also constructs full mapped and heat buffers even though both are discarded. Add checked aggregate source/cell/output-work limits before accumulation, validate non-library layer dimensions as soon as decoded, and avoid allocating unused exact-mode buffers. Cover a repeated-large-layer request with a pre-publication rejection regression.
Clarification: the unchecked expressions are x + w and y + h in atlas reservation validation. Use checked addition or subtraction-based bounds.
Clarification: validate_name accepts digit-leading names, while generated Lua emits bare fields such as 1solid = {...} and M.layers.1far = {...}. Quote generated keys or reject non-Lua identifiers.
Clarification: the lossy conversion is object.size elements cast with as i32 before checked_add; values above i32::MAX become negative.
Clarification: the concrete bad component is a regular file at root/review; the late failing target is review/atlas.png after root-level artifacts have already been replaced.
Clarification: the stale managed file is review/lossy-heatmap.png, and check mode can incorrectly report current after switching the manifest back to exact.
Clarification: load_layers retains one Option of TileKey grid per layer plus lossy heat data; no checked aggregate layer-cell or decoded-work budget exists.

P2 quantize semantics and provenance: atlas.max_colors is applied independently to each layer, so two layers can each select a disjoint palette and the packed atlas can use more indices than its declared color budget. The report also omits max_colors and alpha_threshold, making the policy impossible to audit from provenance. Quantize the scene-wide source set or explicitly redefine the schema as a per-layer budget; for the current atlas-scoped field, enforce that the union of output indices is within the budget and report the parameters, with a two-layer disjoint-color regression.

P2 acceptance evidence: this test proves that a new standalone ribbit-recoil-scene project builds and reports basic classes, but it does not prove the stated replacement or semantic equivalence. The production carts/ribbit-recoil.cart still contains build_level topology substitution and the production environment shell path remains in carts/ribbit-recoil-art/build-environment-atlas.sh. Integrate the compiled subset into the production path or add a regression comparing the compiled five-cell map/class/object results against the production source of truth, then narrow any replacement claim to what is actually retired.

data.reason: Request changes: accepted manifests can overflow atlas arithmetic, bypass object bounds, and generate invalid Lua; output preflight can partially publish on a wrong-type component; aggregate layer memory and atlas-scoped quantize budgets are not bounded correctly. Managed lossy evidence and the claimed RIBBIT replacement also need truthful lifecycle/equivalence coverage. Focused scene tests pass but do not cover these cases.

data.body: Fixed in 285b30f: atlas right/bottom use checked_add and max-u32 reservation regression fails normally before output creation.

Fixed in 285b30f: generated class, tag, and decorative-layer keys use quoted Lua bracket syntax. A digit-leading class/tag/layer fixture now builds, runs, and playtests through the ordinary project path.

Fixed in 285b30f: aggregate retained work is checked at 32,768 cells, non-library map bounds are validated immediately after dimensions, and exact mode no longer allocates discarded mapped/heat buffers. Repeated-large-layer regression rejects before publication.

Fixed in 285b30f: the union of quantized layer output indices is enforced against atlas.max_colors; alpha_threshold and max_colors are included in text/JSON/provenance; two disjoint one-color layers regress the atlas-wide budget.
Fixed in 285b30f: object dimensions use fallible i32 conversion before checked bounds arithmetic, with a u32::MAX regression proving no publication.
Fixed in 285b30f: managed lossy heatmap absence is part of --check and exact recompilation removes stale heat evidence. The lossy-to-exact lifecycle is covered end to end.

Fixed in 285b30f: preflight now rejects symlinks, non-directory intermediates, and directory leaves for every managed path before the first write. Regression preserves sentinel root artifact bytes when review is a regular file.

Fixed in 285b30f: the checked-in slice now compares every named compiled tile's exact pixels and semantic class plus production frog/mutation anchors against ribbit-recoil.cart. README/SPEC explicitly narrow the claim: the boundary is proven, but production topology and legacy atlas builder are not yet retired.
